items.prompt: Match each young animal to its parent.

figure.alt: Four adult animals: a cat, a dog, a hen and a cow.

hints: Young animals grow into adults like their parents.
Do the ones you know first.
Start with the kitten. What does it grow into?
items.explanation: A kitten grows into a cat, a puppy into a dog, a chick into a hen and a calf into a cow.

items.prompt: A baby grows into a child. What does a child grow into?

options.why: Babies are younger than children. Children grow older.
A puppy is a young dog.

hints: Think of your family. Who is older than a child?
Put them in order: baby, child, then who?
items.explanation: A child grows into a teenager and then an adult. People grow and change as they get older.

items.prompt: Put the stages in order, youngest first.
hints: Ask: who is a little older each time?
Put the baby first, then think who comes next.
items.explanation: People grow from a baby to a toddler, then a child, a teenager and an adult.

items.prompt: What is a young duck called?

options.why: A kitten is a young cat.
A cub is a young lion or bear.

hints: The name sounds a bit like its parent.
Many young animal names end in -ling or -let.
Say each word. Which one has duck inside it?
items.explanation: A young duck is called a duckling. It grows into a duck.

items.prompt: Which young animal looks very different from its parent?

figure.alt: A tadpole with a long tail and no legs, and a frog.

options.why: A puppy looks like a small dog.
A kitten looks like a small cat.

hints: Some young animals look like small adults.
Think about which young animal lives in water.
Picture a frog. Does its young one have legs at first?
items.explanation: A tadpole looks very different from a frog. It has a tail and no legs at first, then it changes into a frog.

items.prompt: Does the young animal look like its parent? Sort the cards.
hints: Picture each young animal next to its parent.
Two of these change a lot as they grow.
Start with the caterpillar. What does it become?
items.explanation: Kittens, calves, puppies and lion cubs look like small adults. A caterpillar becomes a butterfly and a tadpole becomes a frog, so they look very different.

items.prompt: What do babies need to grow?

options.why: Babies are too young for homework.
Babies cannot ride bicycles. They need food, sleep and care.

hints: Think about what a baby does all day.
What do all living things need?
Picture a baby at home. What do the adults give it?
items.explanation: Babies need food, such as milk, lots of sleep and care from adults to grow.

items.prompt: A young dog is called a ___.
hints: Think about young dogs you have seen.
A kitten is a young cat. A young dog has its own name.
items.explanation: A young dog is called a puppy. It grows into a dog.

items.prompt: Nadia measures her height on each birthday. What do you notice?

figure.caption: Nadia's height
head: Age
Height
figure.alt: Table of Nadia's height: 100 cm at 4 years, 107 cm at 5 years and 113 cm at 6 years.

options.why: The numbers change each year.
The numbers get bigger, so she is getting taller.

hints: Are the numbers getting bigger or smaller?
items.explanation: Her height goes from 100 cm to 107 cm to 113 cm. The numbers get bigger, so Nadia gets taller as she grows.

items.prompt: Which young animal hatches from an egg?

options.why: Kittens are born from their mother. They do not hatch.
A calf is born from its mother, a cow.

hints: Think about which parent lays eggs.
Birds lay eggs. Which young animal is a baby bird?
Picture a hen sitting on her eggs.
items.explanation: A chick hatches from an egg laid by a hen. Kittens and calves grow inside their mothers and are born.

items.prompt: Wulan finds frogspawn in a pond. What will hatch from it?

options.why: Frogspawn is frog eggs. Fish lay their own eggs.
Snail eggs look different. Frogspawn is frog eggs.

hints: Frogspawn has the word frog in its name.
Think about what a young frog is called.
Ask: what lives in a pond and has a tail at first?
items.explanation: Frogspawn is a group of frog eggs. Tadpoles hatch from it, and the tadpoles grow into frogs.

items.prompt: A caterpillar eats leaves and grows. What will it turn into?

options.why: A caterpillar is a young butterfly or moth. It does not turn into a worm.
Birds hatch from eggs laid by birds.

hints: A caterpillar is a young insect.
Think about what flies near flowers in a garden.
Remember: a caterpillar makes a chrysalis first.
items.explanation: A caterpillar grows, makes a chrysalis and then comes out as a butterfly.

items.prompt: Label how a plant grows.
hints: A plant starts as a seed.
Next, a small plant grows with a few leaves.
At the end it is a big plant.
items.explanation: A seed grows into a seedling and then into a plant.

items.prompt: What is a baby cat called?

options.why: A puppy is a baby dog.
A chick is a baby hen.

hints: A puppy is a baby dog.
items.explanation: A baby cat is a kitten.

items.prompt: What is a baby cow called?

options.why: A lamb is a baby sheep.
A foal is a baby horse.

hints: A lamb is a baby sheep.
items.explanation: A baby cow is a calf.

items.prompt: Which person is the oldest?

options.why: A baby is the youngest.
A child is younger than a grandfather.

items.explanation: A grandfather is the oldest of the three.

items.prompt: A hen sits on her eggs. What hatches out?

options.why: Puppies come from dogs.
Calves come from cows.

hints: A baby hen is a chick.
items.explanation: Chicks hatch from hens' eggs.

items.prompt: What do many baby animals drink from their mothers?

options.why: Mothers do not make juice.
Mothers do not make soup.

items.explanation: Baby cats, dogs, cows and people drink milk from their mothers.

items.prompt: Put the hen's life in order. Start with the egg.
items.explanation: A hen starts as an egg. It hatches into a chick and grows into a hen.

items.prompt: Put the person in order. Start with the youngest.
items.explanation: A person starts as a baby, becomes a child, then an adult and later a grandparent.

items.prompt: Match each animal to its baby.
hints: A foal is a baby horse.
items.explanation: A baby duck is a duckling and a baby horse is a foal. A baby goat is a kid and a baby frog is a tadpole.

items.prompt: Does the baby hatch from an egg or is it born alive?
hints: Pets like cats have babies in a nest.
items.explanation: Hens, ducks and frogs lay eggs. Cats, dogs and cows have babies that are born alive.

items.prompt: Choose all the things a baby needs to grow.
hints: What do you need every day?
A baby cannot ride a bicycle.
items.explanation: Babies need food, sleep and a warm home to grow.

items.prompt: A tadpole grows into a ___. A caterpillar grows into a ___.
hints: A tadpole lives in water first.
items.explanation: A tadpole turns into a frog. A caterpillar turns into a butterfly.

items.prompt: Name the baby animal.
head: Parent
Baby
hints: A baby dog is a puppy.
A chick comes from an egg.
items.explanation: A baby dog is a puppy and a baby cat is a kitten. A baby hen is a chick and a baby cow is a calf.

items.prompt: Baby rabbits are tiny and have no fur. Their mother feeds them milk. After three weeks they have soft fur and hop about. Later they nibble grass.

parts.prompt: What do the baby rabbits grow after three weeks?
What does the mother feed the babies?

items.explanation: The baby rabbits grow soft fur after three weeks. Their mother feeds them milk.

items.prompt: A hen lays 3 eggs. All 3 eggs hatch. How many chicks are there?
items.explanation: Each egg hatches into one chick, so there are 3 chicks.

items.prompt: Tap the baby animal.
hints: A chick is yellow and fluffy.
items.explanation: The chick is the baby. The hen is the parent.

items.prompt: Tap the tadpole.
items.explanation: A tadpole is a baby frog. It has a tail and lives in water.

items.prompt: Label the life of a hen.

figure.alt: An egg, a chick and a hen.

hints: The egg is smooth and oval.
items.explanation: The egg is first, the chick hatches next and the hen is the adult.

items.prompt: A young sheep is called a ___.
hints: It sounds like a woolly animal.
items.explanation: A baby sheep is a lamb.

items.prompt: Draw yourself as a baby and as a child.

criteria.label: Draws a child that is bigger

hints: Add a label to each picture.
items.explanation: A baby grows into a child. A child is taller than a baby.

items.prompt: A small animal with a long tail swims in a pond. It has no legs. Later it has four legs and no tail. What is it?

options.why: A fish does not grow legs.
A snake lives on land.
A duckling has feathers.

items.explanation: A tadpole grows legs and loses its tail when it turns into a frog.

items.prompt: Which one cannot grow up?

options.why: A seed grows into a plant.
A baby grows into a child.
A chick grows into a hen.

items.explanation: A stone is not alive, so it cannot grow up.

items.prompt: Putu is older than Dewi. Dewi is older than baby Eko. Who is the youngest?

options.why: Putu is the oldest.
Eko is younger than Dewi.

options.text: They are all the same age
options.why: They are different ages.

items.explanation: Putu is oldest, Dewi is in the middle and baby Eko is the youngest.
